主要内容: The article discusses the legal challenges faced by insurance companies during the early stages of the coronavirus pandemic. John Houghtaling, a plaintiffs’ lawyer specializing in suing the insurance industry, received a legal memo in mid-March 2020, which outlined arguments insurance carriers planned to use to avoid paying claims related to business interruptions caused by the virus. The memo was circulated among industry insiders who anticipated local government shutdowns. Houghtaling, who was hosting an extravagant dinner with a celebrity chef, was growing increasingly agitated by the document. The memo was part of a broader effort by insurance firms to limit their liability for pandemic-related claims, highlighting the tension between businesses seeking compensation and insurers attempting to avoid payouts under existing policies.
